steps.title: The Floating Workspace 🖱️
steps.description: Grab the top header of the Color Editor to drag it anywhere on your screen. The live preview updates the entire background of the application instantly, giving you full-screen context of how your color choices feel at scale.

steps.title: Solid vs. Gradient Modes 🌓
steps.description: Use the top toggle to switch between a standard solid color and a complex gradient. In Gradient mode, a multi-point slider track appears. Click anywhere on the empty track to add a new color stop. Click and drag the circular handles to adjust the color blending, or use the red trash icon to delete the active stop.

steps.title: Precision Tools & Eyedropper 💉
steps.description: Need to match a brand guideline? Type an exact Hex code into the input field (it fully supports 8-character Hex codes for opacity!). Alternatively, click the Eyedropper icon to sample any color directly from your screen—even outside the browser window. You can also click the quick-swatches below to snap to predefined brand colors.

steps.title: Gradient Formatting 📐
steps.description: When in gradient mode, use the alignment tools to switch between Linear and Radial gradients. For linear gradients, simply type in a custom angle (0-360°) to rotate the color flow exactly how you want it.

steps.title: Export to CSS 📋
steps.description: Once your gradient or solid color is perfect, click the "Copy CSS" button in the center of the screen. The exact rgba() or linear-gradient() CSS string is immediately copied to your clipboard.

cards.title: jQuery Eradication & Signal State 🛑
cards.description: The original implementation relied on querying the DOM (reading data-percent attributes off HTML elements) to calculate gradients. This Angular rewrite abolishes DOM-reading entirely. It uses a strict, unidirectional Signal-based data model. The UI is merely a reflection of the currentHsb() and gradientStops() arrays, resulting in zero-latency updates.

cards.title: Universal Drag Directive 🧲
cards.description: Replacing jQuery UI's draggable physics required building a custom @HostListener directive. To prevent erratic jumping when clicking slider handles, the directive accepts a parent [appDragContainer]. It mathematically binds the mouse/touch clientX and clientY coordinates to the exact bounding rectangle of the track, ensuring flawless 0-100% percentage emissions.

cards.title: Form Integration & ControlValueAccessor 🔌
cards.description: Despite its complexity, the entire editor acts as a standard HTML input. By implementing Angular's ControlValueAccessor, the component seamlessly integrates with Reactive Forms or two-way [(ngModel)] binding. It parses incoming CSS strings back into state, and emits perfectly formatted CSS outwards.

cards.title: Pure Math Color Utilities 🧮
cards.description: Rather than importing bulky color-manipulation libraries, the app utilizes a custom ColorUtils class. It performs complex algebraic conversions between Hex, RGB, and HSB (Hue, Saturation, Brightness) natively. It even reverse-engineers 8-character Hex codes into precise floating-point Alpha channels.
